lessons.what: Shows the full path of the folder you're standing in right now.
lessons.when: You've done 10 cd's and have no idea where you are. pwd is your 'You are here' sign.
lessons.tip: pwd = Print Working Directory.

lessons.what: Lists the files and folders inside a directory.
lessons.when: You open a folder and want to see what's inside, like opening a drawer.
lessons.tip: -a shows hidden files (names starting with a dot).

lessons.what: Moves you into another folder.
lessons.when: Jumping into your project folder to start work, or going back home after.
lessons.tip: .. = one folder up, ~ = home, - = previous folder.

lessons.what: Wipes the terminal screen clean. Your files are safe; only the view resets.
lessons.when: Your screen is full of old output and your brain needs a fresh page.
lessons.tip: Shortcut: Ctrl + L does the same thing.

lessons.man: an interface to the system reference manuals
lessons.what: Opens the official manual for any command.
lessons.when: You forgot what a flag does. Before you google it, ask the manual.
lessons.tip: Inside man: / to search, q to quit.

quiz.q: Which command tells you which folder you are in?
quiz.why: pwd prints your current working directory.

quiz.q: How do you see hidden files with ls?
quiz.why: -a (all) includes names starting with a dot.

quiz.q: What does cd .. do?
Keyboard shortcut that works like clear?
How do you quit a man page?
quiz.why: man uses a pager; q quits it.

lessons.what: Creates an empty file, or updates the time of an existing one.
lessons.when: You need a blank file to start writing notes or code.
lessons.tip: If the file exists, touch won't erase it. Relax.

lessons.what: Creates new folders.
lessons.when: New semester, new folder. Or folders inside folders inside folders.
lessons.tip: -p creates the whole path in one go.

lessons.what: Makes a copy of a file or folder.
lessons.when: Before editing something important, keep a backup copy. Future you says thanks.
lessons.tip: -r is needed to copy a whole folder.

lessons.what: Moves files to another place, or renames them.
lessons.when: Renaming 'final_final_v3.txt' to something less embarrassing.
lessons.tip: Same command for move AND rename.

lessons.what: Deletes files and folders. No recycle bin. Gone is gone.
lessons.when: Cleaning out junk files you'll never need again.
lessons.tip: Use -i while learning: it asks before deleting.

quiz.q: Which command creates an empty file?
quiz.why: touch creates the file if it doesn't exist.

quiz.q: mkdir flag to create nested folders at once?
To copy a whole folder with cp you need...
How do you rename a file?
Which flag makes rm ask before deleting?

lessons.man: concatenate files and print on the standard output
lessons.what: Prints a file's contents on the screen.
lessons.when: Quick peek at a small file without opening an editor.
lessons.tip: -n adds line numbers.

lessons.what: Opens a long file one screen at a time, so you can scroll and search.
lessons.when: The file is 5,000 lines long and cat just dumped it all on you.
lessons.tip: Yes, the man page really says 'opposite of more'.

lessons.man: output the first part of files
lessons.what: Shows the first lines of a file (10 by default).
lessons.when: You only want to see the top of a file, like column names in a CSV.
lessons.tip: -n sets how many lines you want.

lessons.man: output the last part of files
lessons.what: Shows the last lines of a file (10 by default).
lessons.when: Checking the latest messages at the bottom of a log file.
lessons.tip: -f keeps watching for new lines live. Ctrl + C to stop.

lessons.man: print newline, word, and byte counts for each file
lessons.what: Counts lines, words and bytes in a file.
lessons.when: Your essay must be 500 words. Is it? wc knows.
lessons.tip: -l lines, -w words, -c bytes.

quiz.q: Which command prints a whole file to screen?
In less, which key searches?
quiz.why: Type / then the word, press Enter.

quiz.q: head shows how many lines by default?
quiz.why: Both head and tail default to 10.

quiz.q: Which tail flag follows a file live?
quiz.why: -f = follow new lines as they arrive.

quiz.q: How do you count only words?

lessons.what: Prints the username you're logged in as.
lessons.when: Identity crisis? Or just checking if you're the normal user or root.
lessons.tip: With sudo you temporarily become root.

lessons.man: show or set the system's host name
lessons.what: Shows the name of the computer you're using.
lessons.when: You have 3 terminals open on 3 machines. Which one is this?
lessons.tip: The name usually also appears in your prompt.

lessons.man: print or set the system date and time
lessons.what: Shows the current date and time, in any format you like.
lessons.when: Naming a file with today's date so you never lose track.
lessons.tip: +%F gives YYYY-MM-DD, perfect for file names.

lessons.what: Prints a calendar right in the terminal.
lessons.when: How many days until exams? Count them without leaving the terminal.
example: Su Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa
lessons.tip: cal -3 shows last, this and next month. (Install: ncal package)

lessons.man: Tell how long the system has been running.
lessons.what: Shows how long the computer has been on, and how busy it is.
lessons.when: Your laptop feels slow. Has it been on for 40 days straight?
lessons.tip: -p gives a pretty, human-friendly version.

quiz.q: Which command prints your username?
quiz.why: whoami prints the current user name.

quiz.q: hostname shows the name of...
date +%F prints...
cal -3 shows how many months?
uptime -p does what?

lessons.what: Prints text or a variable's value.
lessons.when: Quickly writing a line into a file, or checking what a variable holds.
lessons.tip: >> adds to the end of a file instead of replacing it.

lessons.man: Display or manipulate the history list.
lessons.what: Shows the commands you typed before.
lessons.when: You ran a perfect command yesterday and can't remember it.
lessons.tip: !502 re-runs command number 502. Ctrl + R searches.

lessons.what: Shows where a command's program file lives.
lessons.when: You installed Python twice. Which one actually runs?
lessons.tip: No output = command not found in your PATH.

lessons.what: Tells you what a command really is: a program, alias or shell builtin.
lessons.when: You type ls and it shows colours. Is it secretly an alias?
lessons.tip: Builtins (like cd) live inside the shell itself.

lessons.what: Gives a one-line summary of what a command does.
lessons.when: You see a strange command in a tutorial. What is it, in one line?
lessons.tip: It's the 'trailer' of the man page.

quiz.q: echo "hi" >> notes.txt does what?
!502 does what?
which python3 shows...
type cd says cd is a...
quiz.why: cd is built into the shell.

quiz.q: whatis gives you...
quiz.why: It prints the man page's one-liner.
